cells.tense: You are in the giving and receiving of this moment, and both sides are working.
cells.ask: Name one exchange that's already square, out loud, without adding a tally of what comes next.
cells.core:
There's an exchange moving in front of you — someone offering something, you offering something back — and both sides are landing. You call it normal. It's not. Most people are either carrying a bill or pretending they aren't. You're not. You give when you have it and take when you need it, and the two directions haven't gotten tangled.

Right now fairness isn't a calculation; it's a way of standing near someone. That's rarer than it sounds. It doesn't need protecting with caution. It needs you to notice it, because the next hard week will lean on this, and knowing what it's made of is worth something. Nothing to fix here. One thing to say out loud, before the moment passes and the tally takes over again.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange is square right now, and you didn't have to force it.
cells.verb: Trading fairly with the people in front of you, filling each side of the exchange.
cells.place: What walks in the door right now, before there's time to argue with it.

cells.tense: You are already standing at a future where someone has shorted you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're holding over someone and let it settle today without collecting a word about it.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead of this moment there's a version where it comes out uneven — where you gave more than you got and the bill is live. You're bracing for that version now, and it's shaping how you talk tonight. Every small give is getting weighed. Every silence is getting logged.

The straining is the problem, not the fairness. When you hold a relationship up to a scale that hasn't tipped yet, you're spending energy on a debt that may not come due — and the people around you can feel themselves being counted. Caring about balance is fine. Let the balance breathe. One thing today: set it down and let the answer come on its own time, then see what's actually there when you stop steering it.

cells.tense: You stopped offering at a door you already walked through, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Give one small thing today that costs nothing — a note, a hand, a few minutes — and let it be enough.
cells.core:
There's something in you that hasn't come out in a while. The part that offered got told to wait, and it's still waiting. You're not cold. You're on hold. People can feel that you're near the room but not quite in it with them, and the exchanges around you keep happening without your hand in them.

Done right, this looks ordinary: you hand someone a thing they need, they hand something back, and neither of you is keeping score. What opens it again isn't a big gesture. It's a small, low-stakes give — one thing, to one person, where you don't need anything back. Let one small thing out today and watch what comes back on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You've been holding back the small offers and waiting on the big ones.

cells.tense: You are already keeping the exchange fair here, and calling it something else.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you did today to keep a relationship even, and own it as yours.
cells.core:
Look at today. You softened a reply someone didn't earn. You covered something that would've landed on someone else. You kept a moment from sliding into an argument. That isn't just being polite. That's fairness doing quiet work in real time, between real people.

You'd probably describe it as no big deal, or as just getting along. But it's the same thing that shows up loud when a debt needs settling; here it's running below the surface. Nobody is counting these moments, including you, which is exactly why they hold. Name one of them today as something you did on purpose.
